title: [17/3/2024] The percentage of self employed workers of the total workforce in five countries
prompt: The graph below shows the percentage of self-employed workers of the total workforce in five countries in 1998 and 2008. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart compares the percentages of people who work for themselves in the total workforce across five European countries in 1998 and 2008.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while three countries witnessed rises in their proportions of self-employed workers during this period, the figures for Turkey and Greece showed declining trends. Additionally, despite experiencing the most significant drop, Turkey maintained the highest percentage throughout the period.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at countries with lower proportions, in 1998, the Russian Republic, Slovakia, and the Czech Republic all recorded figures of below 15%, standing at 5%, 7%, and 12%, respectively. The Czech Republic then saw its percentage increase to 15% in 2008, while similar upward trends were seen in Slovakia and the Russian Republic, with their figures rising to 12% and 7% respectively.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding nations with higher proportions, Turkey led the group with about 55% of its workforce being self-employed in 1998, followed by Greece at just over 40%. However, both countries experienced decreases over the next decade, with Turkey's percentage falling to around 38% and Greece's dropping to about 35% by 2008.
